newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur fuel oil barges finish unchanged.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur fuel oil barges finish unchanged.

text.p: NWE high sulphur fuel oil barges ended unchanged on Wednesday after a choppy trading session amid continued problems at Shell's refinery in the Netherlands, traders said.

High sulphur barges traded in the morning as low as $94 and $95 fob ARA, then rose to trade as high as $98 and $99 fob ARA, and traders said ongoing problems at the Shell refinery had boosted the price. The problems are likely to be solved within a week, they said.
Shell bought between eight and ten thousand tonnes of fuel oil during the day, less than on Tuesday.
Prices were strong despite large avails of storage material because of Shell's requirements for refinery-origin material, which traders said was in relatively short supply.
High sulphur cargoes were steady. Interest was still heard coming in from Scotland although no sale had been concluded by the evening, traders said.

Low sulphur fuel oil was broadly stable and the market was quiet. Traders said they had seen a little fresh interest for small pieces to cater for requirements into Italy, but no new signs of new Italian buying.
